liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the Good Lovin' spectacular; Good Lovin' is hot, with Pig playing harmonica [10][17]
- **Good Morning Little School Girl** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the stretch from Schoolgirl down into Lovelight is fiery; Reviewer hears amazing guitar on Schoolgirl, possibly slide [14][18]
- **Attics Of My Life** (2 reviews): Calls Attics rare and says it was the first time it was played; Calls Attics beautiful and describes it as the first one [10][18]
- **New Speedway Boogie** (2 reviews): Names the New Speedway, Nobody's Fault, New Speedway jam as a highlight of the show; Calls the jammed Speedway the kicker, with Jerry singing nastily and riffing between verses, sounding like Pig [9][15]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the Not Fade Away into Lovelight jam is very hot, played at a breakneck tempo; Pig wraps up the show with a sizzling Lovelight after an excellent Not Fade Away jam [9][17]
- **Silver Threads And Golden Needles** (1 review): Silver Threads in the acoustic set is a personal favourite of the reviewer [15]
- **Nobody's Fault But Mine jam** (1 review): Momentum builds around New Speedway, leading into a soulful Nobody's Fault jam [17]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer says this St. Stephen could rival the one on Live/Dead [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-05-14.sbd.warner-evans.28716.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 37 songs; 194 min; rated 3.57/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Uploader describes the sound of this version as excellent [1]
- **gd70-05-14.sbd.cotsman.12439.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min; rated 4.44/5 by 25 [2]. Said about its sound: Levels run a bit low during the acoustic set [18]
- **gd1970-05-14.sbd.cotsman.24223.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1970-05-14.136645.s2.sbd.reelmaster.dat.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 121 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Henry (1st attempt), stage, Whatcha Gonna Do, stage [1]
- Only one drummer plays on this show, Billy, according to the text file [11]
- Reviewer attends the school where the show was held, about two miles from their home [12]
- The show opens with an acoustic set by Jerry and Bob [13]
- Reviewer knows the college where the show was played and was surprised the band played there [14]
- Claims about 90% of the people at this show became lifelong Deadheads [19]
- Reviewer rates this show as not as good as the following night [10]
- Says the show is overshadowed by the following night's, but the reviewer prefers this one [11]
- Reviewer ranks this show alongside the Halloween 1970 show as a favourite 1970 show [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-05-14.sbd.warner-evans.28716.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jack Warner, Marc Evans, Jim Powell; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Most circulating CDRs are partial, many omit the New Riders set, and all lack Fair Chance To Know; This version still lacks most of The Weight, Dire Wolf and the Cold Jordan encore; encoded by Marc Evans [1]
- **gd70-05-14.sbd.cotsman.12439.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dan Capshaw, Walter Schnell and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Chain for acoustic set runs soundboard, master reel, unknown step, DAT, CD, EAC, SHN; electric set omits unknown step; Complete show apart from Dire Wolf and Cold Jordan, which are probably not on the tape [2]
- **gd1970-05-14.sbd.cotsman.24223.shnf**: source: SBD>MR>?>D>CD>EAC>SHN (acoustic set; SBD>MR>D>CD>EAC>SHN (electric set) [3]. Also: Sound Forge was used to fix the pitch of the acoustic set and normalize levels; A slightly higher generation soundboard patches most of Candyman, from 1:37 onward [3]
- **gd1970-05-14.136645.s2.sbd.reelmaster.dat.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Set 2 Source: Soundboard > Reel Master > DAT (48k) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by deadessays.blogspot.com: [The Grateful Dead in St. Louis 1968-1971 (Guest Post)](https://deadessays.blogspot.com/2021/09/the-grateful-dead-in-st-louis-1968-1971.html) [25]
